trails.title: Experiment Record
trails.description: Archived experiment records. The scent on the paper is familiar.

content.text:
Sample No. 001

After consumption, symptoms of excitement appear, extraction efficiency increases by 20%, and the extracted substance is purer. After a second injection of the purification fluid, symptoms of rapid heart rate and high adrenaline secretion occur.

Materials: 3 tables, 7 panes of glass, 2 researchers, and 30 baseball bats.

Sample No. 008

It has been confirmed that its efficacy is positively related to its freshness, and the biochemical substances resulting from the extraction of bodily fluids are in a high-energy state, with active molecular reactions resulting in variable properties. Attempts have been made to control the variables in order to determine a body fluid environment that might render the reagent relatively stable.

*Aside from me, don't even think about touching this thing, unless you want to end up like a certain person who nearly choked on vomit in the lab this morning.

Sample No. 019

After stripping the sucrose from the Picrasma tree leaves, the mixed Picrasma tree suspension is in a state of easy dissociation, and the molecular structure has also become distorted. Perhaps sucrose is one of the keys to stabilizing the output.

Sample No. 023

Sucrose is indeed useful, but its product has not yet reached the expected stability. Attempts have been made to remove alcohol-like compounds from the reagent.

*Stop rushing me, I've had the taste of Picrasma in my mouth for days now!

Sample No. 025

Sucrose, sucrose, sucrose, sucrose, sucrose, sucrose, sucrose, sucrose, alcohol, and Picrasma leaves ... Let's leave it at that for today. We'll see what happens tomorrow.

*Oh! It was preserved! But the effect is extremely weak. Maybe it's time to move the weights on the scale.

...
...
...

Sample No. 053

The ratio for maintaining the effective components of Picrasma sucrose has been basically mastered in an attempt to eliminate its toxicity to humans.

Sample No. 098-A

After dropping 25% Picrasma tree solution on the inner wrists of volunteers (pure humans), 3 volunteers developed itchy, swollen rashes, and 1 volunteer experienced skin ulceration. All recovered without further effects after treatment.

Sample No. 159-C

*What is safe for the human body has no effect on arcanists!

Don't even think about putting these things in human mouths! If you try to use this to pressure us for next year's funding, I'll slap this experiment notebook in your face!

items.text: The Clashing Tides

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Their faces are distorting ... like those paintings ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Is this also some kind of mass hysteria, or ...?
The opera house is bizarrely noisy, and the people within are restless.

items.speaker: Balcony Audience
items.text: Anyone seen my glasses? Could you pass them to me?

items.speaker: Balcony Audience
items.text: Oh, they've grown on my eyes. Don't mind me ...
The cheering crowd stands on their chairs, clapping uncontrollably, shouting with maddened fervor.

items.speaker: Back Audience
items.text: This is Tosca's kiss!

items.speaker: Back Audience
items.text: Come, friends, kith and kin! Take your daggers and get up there! We will all kill our own Scarpia!

items.speaker: Back Audience
items.text: Those so-called upper class people don't deserve the best seats!

items.speaker: Back Audience
items.text: Vissi d'arte, vissi d'amore!
More and more people leave their seats, some shouting as they step up and over to lean over railings and into the aisles.
The music still plays, and the curtain has yet to fall.

items.speaker: Guest in Box
items.text: Splendid! I can almost feel the blood splashing on my face!

items.speaker: Guest in Box
items.text: There is no doubt this is art! The way in which reality replaces fantasy ... I've never seen a show like this before ...

items.speaker: Guest in Box
items.text: Selah, Orff, what happened? Have you got blood on your faces, too? Is this part of the show, or ...?

items.speaker: Guest in Box
items.text: Woww!
The crowd blends like a thick oil paint, surging and washing over every corner of the opera house.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: They're killing each other in a frenzy! Is no one noticing this?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Madam Hofmann, I have an emergency here. I ...
Marcus stumbles, knocked over by the frenzied crowd, and the connection to her communicator is lost.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No, I can't hear anything!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The crowd won't let me leave ... I need to make way myself!
Someone rushes out from the shadows, drawing a sidearm.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Quiet, be quiet!

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Go to hell, you terrorists!
If their arrival had meant to bring order, it succeeded only in making the scene that much more chaotic.
Gunshots, screams, roars, and bellows meld together.
A few staff members from the Foundation branch weave through the crowd, but they are either infected with hysteria or swept away in the flood of people.
Marcus dodges awkwardly among them, like a leaf in a rushing river.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I need to ... I need to disperse them. At least open up the exit ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ugh!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, what are you doing?! I said evacuate!!
Hofmann hurries from the other side of the curtain, pulling Marcus away from the swarming crowd.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But people are dying! It is our duty to ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I just got a message from the headquarters.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The Timekeeper has issued a twenty-four hour "Storm" warning.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... What?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The Manus has carried out several assassinations on the same day. The instability of this era has reached the Critical Point.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ... Which means the "Storm" is coming.
Marcus collapses to the ground.
Slowly, bewilderedly, she begins raking her hands through her hair.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: N-no ... No way ... The "Storm" ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It was me ... It was me ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It was me who started the chain reaction ... It was me who leaked out the details of the island ... It was me!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Get a hold of yourself, Marcus!
A pair of strong hands pull her up from the ground.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: This is the "Storm" of time. Compared to the chaos it causes, you and I mean nothing more than a pebble.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: It happened many times before you did anything, and it will happen countless times more.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The eras in history will disappear again and again, and so will the people. The situation can't get any worse.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The only thing we can do now is to find the ritual that grants immunity to the "Storm." It's the only way to save more lives!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The Foundation has issued the evacuation notice. All staff must return to the headquarters before the "Storm" arrives.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The closest evacuation point is Vienna Central Station. They'll pick us up there in two hours.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Two hours?
Marcus recalls the map she saw on her way with picture clarity.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It takes less than two hours to get ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I know. There are still things we can do, before the "Storm" truly arrives.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But the enemies are probably much stronger than we are, and there will be no backup for us.
Not far away, the head of the Vienna branch lies slain, his face wrenched in horror, a testament to a crime.
Below the stage, people in fancy dress, in uniform, in costume, roar and surge about, forming an indistinguishable mass.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: You once told me what really scared you was not the threat to your life, but the possibility of dying ignorant.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I think ... I understand what you mean now.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I don't want that either ... I don't want to go back to the headquarters without doing anything at all!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Well said, Marcus. Let's go.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Find Heinrich and Isolde. They might know the ritual, or have the clues we need.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: We can still catch the last train if everything goes smoothly.
Hofmann expertly loads her weapon again, and Marcus grips her lamp tightly.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Kakania is not with you?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mmm, Ms. Kakania ran up to the stage. She and Isolde ...
Beyond the shoulders of the crowd, the green figure has disappeared from the stage.
Marcus squints, inspecting the curtains and stage props.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Heinrich has enchanted all the props. There must be a hidden entrance to the secret chamber.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I am sure ... Ms. Kakania and Isolde are still in this theater!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Come here!
The deep purple glow of an incantation radiates from the darkness.
Hofmann pulls Marcus back by the shoulder. The incantation flies past her hair, singeing it.
The familiar figure of a gentleman flits into the scene.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Heinrich!
A foot almost steps on air.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Ugh, there are traps under the floor!
This opera is silent.
No audience, no music, not a word or note from any actors.
A space to think.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Isolde!
Cries echo from behind the curtain.
She opens her eyes as another protagonist leaps onto the stage.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Doctor.
TO BE CONTINUED…
